methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a single-centre retrospective cohort (n=203 SBM-HSPC patients, Qingdao University Hospital, 2017-2023) with high-quality imaging validation (dual-modality ECT + CT/MRI with dual-radiologist review). Cox proportional hazards regression is appropriately applied for survival analysis. The landmark analysis at 3 and 6 months to evaluate NHA timing effects with immortal time bias mitigation is a methodological strength. Variables with p<0.2 in univariate analysis were included in multivariate models without stepwise selection, which is appropriate. Limitations include single-centre design, retrospective data, absence of performance status data, limited sample sizes in docetaxel subgroups (n=12 at 3 months), and incomplete PSA continuous data (categorical only for >70% of patients), which explains the paradoxical high-PSA survival association.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective single-centre cohort study (Oxford LoE 4) addressing a clinically important question about optimal timing of NHA initiation in SBM-HSPC—a high-risk patient group in which early intensive therapy is guideline-endorsed but timing data from Chinese centers are limited. The landmark analysis finding of 45% mortality reduction with early NHA (within 3 months, HR 0.55) directly supports clinical practice prioritization. The 6.09% SBM-HSPC incidence estimate provides the first contemporary data from a developed Chinese regional center, representing a major reduction from 54% historical estimates and informing staging workup policy in China.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports patient selection criteria, variable definitions (CHAARTED criteria, SRE adjudication, landmark analysis methodology), statistical methods, and key limitations. The landmark analysis methodology is clearly described with explicit patient-level exposure assignment rules. The paradoxical high-PSA survival finding is explicitly flagged as potentially confounded and hypothesis-generating. Ethics approval and consent waiver are documented. Limitations include absence of publicly available data (single-institution records), no code sharing, and incomplete reporting of performance status—a key prognostic variable not included in models. Missing data handling (complete case analysis, <5% missing) is described.

novelty_literature.justification: The study provides the first contemporary incidence data for SBM-HSPC from a developed Chinese regional center (6.09%), demonstrating convergence with Western figures and a dramatic decline from 2008 estimates (54%). The landmark analysis confirming early NHA benefit in a Chinese SBM-HSPC cohort extends LATITUDE/TITAN/ENZAMET trial findings to real-world practice with a methodologically rigorous immortal-time-bias-free approach. The identification of HDV as the dominant prognostic factor in this 83.7% HDV-enriched cohort, and the null results for docetaxel and bone-targeting agents in terms of OS, add clinically relevant context specific to this high-risk Chinese patient group.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript communicates its central findings clearly and the landmark analysis rationale is well-explained. The discussion of the paradoxical high-PSA survival finding demonstrates appropriate scientific caution. However, writing quality is uneven—some sections contain informal phrasing, speculative passages with limited evidence support, and the introduction mixes epidemiological context with mechanistic claims loosely tied to the primary analysis. The supplementary tables addressing exclusion vs inclusion group comparability strengthen confidence in cohort completeness. The conclusion is appropriately focused on actionable clinical messages.

key_strengths: Landmark analysis methodology effectively mitigates immortal time bias in assessing NHA timing effects—a methodological improvement over most retrospective prostate cancer treatment timing studies
First contemporary Chinese regional incidence data for SBM-HSPC (6.09%), demonstrating convergence with Western rates and informing national policy on staging practices
High-quality imaging validation (dual-modality ECT+CT/MRI with dual-radiologist review) ensures reliable metastasis classification per CHAARTED criteria
Explicit acknowledgment and discussion of the paradoxical PSA association demonstrates scientific integrity and model transparency
key_concerns: Single-centre design with n=203 limits statistical power for subgroup analyses, particularly docetaxel (n=12 at 3-month landmark) and intermediate Gleason subgroups with unstable estimates
Absence of ECOG performance status data in the Cox models is a major unaddressed confounder likely influencing NHA selection and survival
Retrospective design introduces treatment selection bias—patients assigned NHA vs ADT alone likely differed systematically in clinical fitness and institutional resource access
Informal and speculative writing in several discussion passages (e.g., 'golden window' framing for ages 60-74) weakens scientific credibility relative to the solid analytical core
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically competent retrospective cohort study using landmark analysis to provide real-world evidence for early NHA initiation benefit in Chinese SBM-HSPC, with valuable contemporary incidence data; single-centre design and missing performance status confounder are manageable through explicit limitation framing, supporting tier 3 publication with minor revisions primarily addressing writing quality and confounding discussion.
